summary: Defines the three-level resource namespace (Application -> Registry [registry_def] -> Record) that authorization grants will bind to. Pins entity schemas, scoped-uniqueness rules, FK integrity, the grant-binding surface (three reference shapes), system-registry flag, and 17 acceptance criteria. Fully inherits T-0013 tenant-isolation invariants.
functional: Exactly three namespace levels in fixed order: Application -> Registry (registry_def) -> Record; no other shape permitted
application entity: (tenant_id, slug) scoped-unique per tenant; slug URL-safe; deletion blocked when registries exist
registry_def entity: (tenant_id, application_id, slug) scoped-unique; carries record_schema jsonb (JSON Schema); FK to application within same tenant; is_system flag
record entity: identified by (tenant_id, id); data jsonb validated against parent registry_def.record_schema at write time; FK to registry_def within same tenant
All FKs have tenant_id as leading column; cross-tenant FKs structurally impossible
Grant-binding surface: three reference shapes — application-level, registry-level, record-level; all UUIDs immutable on rename
System registries (is_system=true) visible, grantable, protected from tenant-admin deletion
non_functional: Full T-0013 tenant isolation on all three tables: tenant_id NOT NULL leading PK, ENABLE+FORCE RLS, default-DENY, withTenant, scoped uniqueness
record_schema jsonb enables schema evolution without DDL; no separate registry_type discriminator in MVP
Application/registry/record UUIDs stable across renames — grant bindings survive slug/display_name changes
tenant_id leading index column on all composite indexes
No orphaned rows: structural FK enforcement + delete-blocking at API layer
out_of_scope: Grant/authority model (grant table, roles, permission resolution) — T-0018
UI / REST API endpoint definitions for CRUD
Record-level access control enforcement logic — T-0018
Flowable process integration with registry records — T-0015/Etap 2
Keycloak/identity provisioning beyond tenant_id JWT claim
Agent registry product feature schema — Etap 2

acceptance_criteria.text: For every table in {application, registry_def, record}: relrowsecurity AND relforcerowsecurity = true. Zero exceptions.
INSERT tenant_id=NULL into any of the three tables raises NOT NULL violation.
No SET LOCAL choros.tenant_id, SELECT count(*) each table as choros_app returns 0 (default-DENY).
Context=tenant_A, SELECT count(*) WHERE tenant_id=tenant_B returns 0 on all three tables.
Two tenants may each have application.slug='procurement'; duplicate within same tenant raises unique violation.
Two applications in one tenant may each have registry_def.slug='requests'; duplicate within (tenant_id,application_id) raises unique violation.
INSERT registry_def with application_id not in application for same tenant_id raises FK violation.
INSERT record with registry_id not in registry_def for same tenant_id raises FK violation.
For every FK on registry_def and record, tenant_id is at position 1. T-0013 FF-5 probe extended to new tables.
Updating application.slug does not change application.id; registry_def rows remain valid via FK.
Updating registry_def.slug does not change registry_def.id; record rows remain valid via FK.
DELETE application with registry_def children raises FK violation or API-rejected; no orphaned rows.
DELETE registry_def with record children raises FK violation or API-rejected; no orphaned rows.
Tenant-admin API DELETE on registry_def is_system=true rejected with explicit error.
Static schema lint confirms the three grant-binding reference shapes are constructable from column defs — no missing UUID column.
known_tenant_tables CI fixture from T-0013 FF-2 extended to include application, registry_def, record; CI fails if any lacks FORCE RLS.
INSERT record with data non-conformant to parent registry_def.record_schema rejected at app layer; conformant accepted.
